description: QUALIFY with the window function written INLINE in the predicate rather than referenced through a SELECT alias - QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY v DESC) = 1. The engine precomputes each inline window function over all rows and substitutes it before filtering. Pinned with an equality (top row per group), a range predicate (top two per group), an AND against an ordinary predicate, and the alias-based form that already worked, as a regression guard. Converted 1:1 from query/QualifyInlineWindowTest (now retired); the Java asserted row counts and read the first column by index, so the converted tests pin the whole row set - the top-two and alias tests had asserted only a COUNT, which four or two arbitrary rows would have satisfied.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE w (id INTEGER, grp VARCHAR, val INTEGER)
SELECT id FROM w QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY grp ORDER BY val DESC) = 1
CREATE TABLE w (id INTEGER, grp VARCHAR, val INTEGER)
SELECT id FROM w QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY grp ORDER BY val DESC) <= 2
CREATE TABLE w (id INTEGER, grp VARCHAR, val INTEGER)
SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY grp ORDER BY val DESC) AS rn FROM w QUALIFY rn = 1
CREATE TABLE w (id INTEGER, grp VARCHAR, val INTEGER)
SELECT id FROM w QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY grp ORDER BY val DESC) = 1 AND grp = 'a'
